captions.text: B : « Je ne peux pas tout porter. »

shoe_layer.note: k 0-95: wide layer (L-S4 push-in vs E-S3 static wide: same file, different camera, so the screen raster differs by the push-in only); k 96-149: hi layer in the identical close camera (L-S5 = E-S4 as a function of time since the cut), screen raster byte-identical before the whole-pixel water-level translation dy_screen = round(m * dy_world), which rides each version's own water level.

declared: edit-r3: U1's water() and plank() are replaced at run time by the editor's versions (compose.py unedited): the water plate is reflect-tiled downward (no edge-clamp streaks) and carries a uniform 0.72 lighting gain in the closes; the card plank bends along an elastic point-load curve, drawn with SAG_X = 2.5 times the trace's deflection beyond its 2 px resting sag (the occupant's FK root is lowered by the same extra sag), and the water's own plate rows are laid translucently over any part of the card bent below the water line. Ledger values are the trace's.
edit-r3: the last crossings (L-S8, and E-S6 from local 24.0) push in at P2 from m 0.955 to m 1.38.

edit-r3: the L-S5/E-S4 close ends 16 px lower (centre (200,352)); the L-S6 two-shot is centred (150,244) at M 2.2; in L-S6 B's free far arm is re-keyed (open palm at chest height) for local 20.4-21.75 (no grip involved).

edit-r3: the shoe in B's hand hangs by its heel counter, upright within 0.3 s of the grasp, layered over the mitten with the mitten's thumb card re-laid over the heel; a bag held at head height is layered behind the holder's head.

edit-r3: the close's P1 plane behind the hand-off is the fluted Mekong trunk (already credited) instead of Buttress Roots 1; the closes' depth-blur sigmas are smaller (P0 0.8, P1 0.35, near 0.6, near_fg 1.1); the near-bank ledger placard is removed; sweat glints are L 246-248 on a damp patch, and B's face gains a pencilled ear and jaw line.

edit-r2: the E-S3/E-S4 and E-S4/E-S5 cuts are 0.5 s later than plan section 6 (50.5 and 52.9 instead of 50.0 and 52.4) so that E-S4 starts at the same shoe-layer frame and the same time before the hand-off as L-S5; E-S5 is 1.6 s (the rewrite is written faster); E-S6 and every other cut are as planned. The film-to-local offset of E is unchanged (39.5 s).

edit-r2: the L-S5/E-S4 close opens on the hand-off with both heads in frame and tilts down with B's kneel to the plank-foot framing; the heart leaf that hid the receiver is removed from the near dressing; a fluted buttress trunk (edit-r3: the Mekong trunk cut, replacing Buttress Roots 1) stands as a P1 plane behind the hand-off.
edit-r2: charcoal mud and sweat glints are laid on faces and mittens by the editor's wet pass (handmade make-up on the card puppets); the shoe is never touched by it.
edit-r2: the splash on the last crosser's shins is a handmade cut-paper water sheet and card droplets, animated on twos from the minimum-clearance frame of the trace.

E-S1/E-S2 show the L frames (byte-identical, plan section 6). U2's E trace differs there (C 10 px left, water 2 px lower); the E world takes over at the cut into E-S3 (45.5 s), after the ledger insert.
The ledger inserts are hands only: in L the strike and rewrite are made by B's free left hand (A has crossed), in E by A's free left hand.
The shoe's dryness and whiteness is the one declared impossibility.
